title: Find Triangular Sum of an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, where each element is a digit from 0 to 9, the triangular sum is found by repeatedly creating a new array where each element is the sum modulo 10 of consecutive elements from the previous array, until only one element remains.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, where each element is a digit from 0 to 9, the triangular sum is found by repeatedly creating a new array where each element is the sum modulo 10 of consecutive elements from the previous array, until only one element remains. This final element is the triangular sum.
constraints: Every input value is a digit from zero through nine.
Replace the current row by adjacent pair sums modulo ten.
Repeat until one digit remains, and return that digit.
hints: Each round is a direct simulation of the definition.
Keep only the current row; the prior row is unnecessary after producing all adjacent sums.
While the row has more than one value, replace it with pair sums modulo ten.
Every loop produces exactly the next defined row and decreases its length by one, so termination returns the required final digit.
editorial: Every loop produces exactly the next defined row and decreases its length by one, so termination returns the required final digit.

tests.explanation: A one-element row is already reduced, so its triangular sum is five.
